study.title: Unsupervised deep learning for the matching of vascular anatomy in multiple digital subtraction angiograms
study.venue: Medical Imaging 2024: Image Perception, Observer Performance, and Technology Assessment (Proc. SPIE Vol. 12929)

imaging.modality_detail: Digital subtraction angiography image sequences; individual diagnostic frames (plus d=2 neighbouring frames) used
imaging.territory_detail: Abdominopelvic arteries: celiac trunk / common, proper, left and right hepatic arteries; lower abdominal aorta and common, internal and external iliac arteries

annotation.annotator_expertise: Interventional radiologist with four years of attending experience (labeled series anatomic location and diagnostic frames)

task.task_description: Unsupervised matching of DSA frames from different sequences showing anatomically neighbouring vessels using two parallel VGG encoders trained with NCE contrastive loss on synthetic mother-daughter crops, then localizing/aligning the daughter image within the mother image via convolution of encodings into a response map with rotation search.
task.clinical_application: Aiding interventional proceduralists in localizing DSA image sequences relative to prior sequences during endovascular procedures

temporal_evidence.quote: synthetic matches, which were made by taking a single frame of an image sequence, duplicating that frame, and cropping it at a random location

G1.quote: There was a limited number of 42 patients that had series of images taken of blood vessels that were anatomically matching

G3.quote: Future research may focus on extending this method from matching image frames to matching image sequences

G5.quote: Given that this method is unsupervised, it could be used to pre-train a network using a synthetic dataset, followed by training on labeled data

G7.quote: the implementation of explainable artificial intelligence could enhance the interpretation of image localization

other_limitations: Real-world localization only qualitatively assessed because acquisition coordinates were lost during anonymization
Localization fails when prominent artifacts appear in both images
Small real-world batch size due to few unique patients
future_work: Extend matching from image frames to image sequences
Reduce matching sensitivity to image artifacts
Use unsupervised synthetic pre-training followed by training on labeled data
Add explainable AI (visual and textual/conceptual explanations)
